_: One pixel of a shrub, one layer switched off at a time. The bush's three layers — the heart, the
shell of cut-out leaf over it, and the leaf cards standing on the shell — are all the same leaf in
three states, and for five sessions the wrong one of them was the brightest: the cards, which the sun
actually reaches, painted (47,83,13) while the shell behind them painted (70,114,20). The cases below
are the ones that settled where that came from. The mirror on a smooth shell is what made it bright:
`specularIntensity` on the shell and the heart alone moved the shell thirty-nine points of light and
moved the cards not at all, while forcing every card's normal square at the sun bought six and turning
the scene's shadows off bought nothing.
Run it with: node tools/lights.js tools/bushface.json

cases.name: shell hidden — what the cards are on their own
cases.js: for (const m of scene.meshes) if (m.material && m.material.name === 'bushEdge') m.isVisible = false;

cases.name: cards hidden — the shell in their place
cases.js: for (const m of scene.meshes) if (m.material && m.material.name === 'bushLeaf') m.isVisible = false;
